floating_regions.meaning: Studio's support-necessity detector found sharp-tail regions when support was unavailable. This is not the same test as the MCP's nominal-layer floating-island heuristic.
next_steps: Inspect the named object's underside and earliest affected layers in the highlighted geometry preview and Studio Preview.
Compare reorientation or a supported candidate. Check whether supports can reach the region; support paint alone does not enable supports.
For a moving joint, preserve mating clearances and compare a small cut-out test piece before the full print.

floating_cantilever.meaning: Studio's support-necessity check found a cantilever beyond its native distance criterion while support was unavailable. That criterion is not a universal printable bridge limit.
next_steps: Inspect the cantilever underside and support reachability. Compare reorientation or a supported revision against the unchanged baseline.

phrases: support enforcers are used but support is not enabled
support_enforcers_disabled.pattern: ^support enforcers are used but support is not enabled\.
support_enforcers_disabled.meaning: Studio found an enforcer volume or painted support enforcer on an object without active support. Painting an enforcer does not itself switch support on.
next_steps: Read enable_support and support_type at project and object scope; inspect enforcer volumes and painted supports.
Enable the intended support mode in a new revision, or remove unwanted enforcers. Re-slice and verify generated support paths.

If saved settings disagree with the GUI after reopening, save the GUI project under a new filename and reopen that exact file in MCP. Compare overrides; unsaved GUI state and preset reloads are not synchronized.

support_incomplete.meaning: Studio's tree-support coverage check found significant overhang regions without support. Enabling supports alone does not establish coverage.
next_steps: Inspect blockers, painted regions and whether supports can reach the underside.

If the native message names build-plate-only, compare disabling support_on_build_plate_only in a new revision. Check support removal, cosmetic contact and moving-part clearances before choosing the candidate.

phrases: can't be printed for empty layer
empty_gcode_layers.pattern: ^object can't be printed for empty layer between
empty_gcode_layers.meaning: Studio found empty extrusion layers between printable layers. Thin sections or a faulty mesh can be responsible; the native message may include Z ranges and several objects.
next_steps: Inspect the native Z ranges, mesh integrity and section thickness against the installed nozzle's line width and layer height.
Repair or thicken the design, or compare compatible finer layers or wall-generation settings. Do not treat an empty-layer warning as solved by adding infill.

limitations: The rules describe the pinned source version. A different GUI version requires version-specific verification.
English message recognition is heuristic. Unknown or translated messages remain unknown and retain their original text.
Native warnings generally do not provide feature coordinates. Geometry links are related candidates, not confirmed native warning locations.
The CLI result retains only the last warning per plate. Job-log warning records can recover additional messages, but missing records never establish that a warning is resolved.
No diagnosis proves physical fit, strength, surface finish or successful support removal.
